articles.title: US Open: No. 3 seed Felix Auger-Aliassime upset by Karen Khachanov in second round
articles.summary: Auger-Aliassime said he was "dizzy and seeing spots" while playing after the match.
articles.body:
The US Open draw did No. 3 seed Felix Auger-Aliassime no favors by setting him up with Karen Khachanov in the second round. His body didn't do him many favors Thursday, either.

One of the more intriguing early matchups at Flushing Meadows ended with the unseeded Khachanov celebrating a 6-7, 6-3, 6-2, 6-2 win over the Canadian star, who appeared to be dealing with some physical discomfort during the match. Khachanov will face the winner of No. 32 seed Ignacio Buse and Benjamin Bonzi in the third round.

The 30-year-old Khachanov was not just another unseeded opponent. He might be ranked only No. 50 in the world now, but the veteran is a former top-10 player who reached the US Open semifinal in 2022 and has reached at least the third round in seven of his past eight Grand Slams.

He looked like a challenge for Auger-Aliassime from the start, taking him to a tiebreak after exchanging two breaks in the first set. Auger-Aliassime pulled that out, but had little success for the rest of the match.

Auger-Aliassime is usually one of the best servers on tour, and yet had to face 20 break points over the course of the match. He committed far more unforced errors as well, 47 to Khachanov's 30, and seemed to be diminished in general as the match went on.

He couldn't provide an exact diagnosis while speaking with reporters after the match, but described some symptoms:

"I just couldn't feel well and was dizzy and seeing spots. Yeah, couldn't recover. I thought maybe it would pass, but it didn't … Karen's a great player. I cannot beat him or anybody in this draw feeling the way I felt today."

It also sounded like the issue came out of nowhere:

"I've had cramps before, I felt OK. Tired towards the end of matches, but in a normal way. This was abnormal a little bit. And there was no signs in the last couple of days and no signs this morning as well. I'm not sure. I'm going to run some tests and see what comes out of it."

Combine all of that with some vintage form from Khachanov and the Canadian was facing a problem he couldn't solve.

Khachanov acknowledged Auger-Aliassime's issues in his postmatch interview:

"I'm not sure, I saw that maybe he had some physical issues. I guess it's part of our sport, part of tennis. I wish him to feel better, speedy recovery if he's injured, I don't know. What I can say from my side is I tried to give my best performance."

Auger-Aliassime reached the quarterfinal at Roland-Garros and Wimbledon this year and has reached the semifinal at the US Open in both 2021 and 2025.

It's also the latest bit of chaos in the men's draw, which saw No. 4 seed Novak Djokovic go down in the first round , as well as rising stars No. 10 Arthur Fils and No. 12 Rafael Jodar.

Even the top two players face question marks, as No. 1 Alexander Zverev needed a comeback in five sets to survive the first round , while No. 2 Carlos Alcaraz, who is playing his first tournament in more than four months, dropped his first set on Wednesday .

articles.title: Nick Kyrgios suspended for one month after cocaine positive at Mallorca event
articles.summary: Tennis News: Nick Kyrgios has accepted a one-month suspension after testing positive for cocaine at a tournament in Spain in June, the International Tennis Integri.
articles.body: Nick Kyrgios has accepted a one-month suspension after testing positive for cocaine at a tournament in Spain in June, the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) announced on Thursday.The 31-year-old Australian had been provisionally suspended since August 4, although the development was only made public more than two weeks later.According to the ITIA, Kyrgios told investigators that he had used cocaine socially during a night out before he was scheduled to compete in Mallorca. After consulting an expert from the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA), he accepted that the substance had been used outside of competition.Under WADA's rules, the default suspension for such an offence is three months. However, the ban can be reduced to one month if the player completes a treatment programme. The ITIA said Kyrgios' suspension expires on Thursday, subject to him completing the required programme.The Australian will also lose the prize money and ranking points he earned at the Mallorca tournament. Kyrgios was beaten in his only match there by fellow Australian Adam Walton.The latest setback adds to a difficult period for Kyrgios, who has featured in just four ATP singles matches this year. The 31-year-old is currently ranked 918th in the world.Kyrgios enjoyed the biggest run of his career at Wimbledon in 2022, reaching the final before losing to Novak Djokovic.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘You have to respect the sport’: Naomi Osaka calls out USTA over influencer culture at US Open
articles.summary: Tennis News: Naomi Osaka has called for better management of influencers attending the US Open, saying their presence can help grow tennis but should not come at t.
articles.body: Naomi Osaka has called for better management of influencers attending the US Open, saying their presence can help grow tennis but should not come at the expense of respecting the sport's rules and etiquette.The four-time Grand Slam champion spoke about the issue after advancing to the third round with a 6-2, 5-7, 6-1 victory over Katerina Siniakova on Thursday.The USTA has invited a large number of influencers to the tournament as part of its efforts to broaden tennis's reach and connect with new audiences. Osaka acknowledged the potential benefits but believes there needs to be greater awareness among those attending matches."If you come to a sporting event, you have to respect the sport. I feel like it’s common courtesy to read up on the sport. Especially the etiquette," Osaka said.She added that bringing influencers into the tournament can introduce tennis to audiences who may not otherwise follow the sport."It could be a good thing for people to make the sport of tennis popular to their specific audience. But I think it has to be managed a lot better, especially in the situation like in my first round match."‘You want people to continue to grow the sport’Osaka stressed that she is not against efforts to expand tennis's audience. Instead, she believes that growth should come alongside an understanding of how to behave at matches."Overall there’s huge positives. You want people to continue to grow the sport. I just think it has to be in a way that everyone knows the rules & the etiquette."Her comments come as the US Open continues to attract attention from audiences beyond traditional tennis fans, with influencers becoming an increasingly visible presence at major sporting events.Osaka survives Siniakova scareOsaka's comments came after she recovered from a mid-match lapse to reach the third round. The No. 13 seed raced through the opening set in 30 minutes and moved 4-2 ahead in the second, but her level dropped sharply as she committed 20 unforced errors after making only four in the first set.Siniakova took the second set 7-5, but Osaka quickly regained control in the decider. She broke for a 2-0 lead before completing a 6-1 final set."The match was definitely really tough and I don’t know, I just felt like I had to fight," Osaka said. "I definitely had a couple opportunities in the second set and I think I was a little bit too hard on myself. So I took the bathroom break, regrouped a little, came back and just tried to have no regrets."Eala, Gauff also advanceAlex Eala also booked her place in the third round after defeating Oleksandra Oliynykova 6-1, 6-4. The No. 17 seed from the Philippines enjoyed strong support from the crowd and said she was proud to represent her country.Coco Gauff, the 2023 US Open champion, progressed after beating Paula Badosa 6-4, 7-6 (5), while 2022 champion Iga Swiatek and 2025 runner-up Amanda Anisimova were among the other winners.Madison Keys survived a major scare, saving five match points before edging Anna Bondar 5-7, 6-4, 7-6 (10-5).On the men's side, Felix Auger-Aliassime became the highest-seeded player to exit so far, losing to Karen Khachanov after struggling with dizziness and vision problems.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Nick Kyrgios: Former Wimbledon finalist accepts one-month suspension from International Tennis Integrity Association for testing positive for cocaine
articles.summary: Nick Kyrgios has accepted ‌and served a reduced, one-month suspension under anti-doping rules after testing positive ‌for cocaine; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app
articles.body:
Kyrgios, who had been ​provisionally suspended since August 4, had ‌entered into a treatment programme approved by the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) to ​reduce the three-month default suspension under WADA rules.

The Australian gave a sample at an ATP tournament in Majorca in June which tested positive for benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine.

The drug is banned in competition and the former Wimbledon finalist has been provisionally suspended since August 4, meaning he cannot play or attend tournaments.

During an ​interview with ITIA investigators, the 31-year-old ⁠explained that his use ⁠of cocaine had "occurred socially" during a night out before he was due ‌to play in Mallorca, the statement said.

The ITIA consulted an independent scientific expert at a ‌World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA)-accredited laboratory, who stated that the explanation was consistent with the level of cocaine found in his sample.

"As a result, the ITIA accepted ⁠that Kyrgios' use of cocaine was ​outside of competition," it added.

The ITIA ​said Kyrgios' suspension ends on Thursday, ​subject to completion of the programme.

Prize money and ⁠ranking points from the Mallorca event will be forfeited.

Cocaine is prohibited in-competition and carries a ⁠provisional suspension.

Kyrgios apologised last month ​on social media for the failed drug ​test, saying he had made a "huge mistake" and took full responsibility for ‌it.

"I made a huge mistake and I take full responsibility for it," Kyrgios said in a post on Instagram.

"I'm sorry to my fans, my family, my sponsors and everyone close to me. Above all, I'm sorry to the kids who follow me. I know the example this sets and I'm deeply disappointed in myself."

His first-round loss to fellow Australian Adam Walton in Majorca was his last competitive singles outing and one of only four singles matches he has played this season.

Sky Sports Tennis' Annabel Croft described Kyrgios as a "tormented soul" who could now find himself on the receiving end of the very criticism he dished out when Jannik Sinner and Iga Swiatek were involved in high-profile doping cases.

"He has always struck me as a tormented soul out there, and he is never far from creating headlines," Croft said. "He seems to do that effortlessly.

"There is a lot of criticism being thrown at him right now because he was the one firing arrows at other players who had been banned for a certain amount of time. It is now being directed right back at him."

Former world No 40 Ryan Harrison believes Kyrgios must strike the right balance between his responsibilities on the court and his downtime off it.

"It is disappointing," Harrison added. "Kyrgios has been such an electric player for so long.

"He is one of those guys. You talk about the 'Big Four', and he was the next in line that the casual fan and observer would talk about because of the way he played, his talent, fearlessness and energy.

"The persona would come out sometimes in the way he handled pressure. Sometimes it wasn't always positive.

"When you are an athlete and training on a regular basis, your life is very structured and regimented.

"When you stop playing and you are not doing that on a week-to-week basis, some players can find it difficult to strike a balance and know, 'When can I go out?'

"I think Nick needs to find that balance and, while it is disappointing, hopefully for his sake, as he takes time away, he can find happiness off the court and be the best he can be."

2013: Turns professional after winning the Australian Open boys' singles title in January of that year

2014: Announces himself to the world on his Wimbledon debut by upsetting world No 1 Rafael Nadal in the fourth round when just 19 years old.

July 2015: Criticised for his behaviour and comments at Wimbledon, including accusations of 'tanking' in fourth-round loss to Richard Gasquet.

August 2015: Fined and given 28-day suspended ban for controversial comments about Stan Wawrinka's then-girlfriend, women's player Donna Vekic.

October 2016: Criticised for his effort during a defeat to Mischa Zverev at Shanghai Masters. Receives an eight-week suspension, which was later reduced.

October 2016: Reaches his career-high singles ranking of 13th in the world in October after claiming his first three of seven career ATP titles in the same year - wins in Marseille, Atlanta, and Tokyo.

June 2018: Fined for inappropriate behaviour during Queen's semi-final match against Marin Cilic after TV cameras caught him using his water bottle to simulate a lewd act during a changeover.

May 2019: Throws a chair onto the court during the Rome Masters and is defaulted from his match against Casper Ruud.

January 2022: Wins the Australian Open men's doubles title with fellow Australian and good friend Thanasi Kokkinakis.

July 2022: Reaches his first Grand Slam singles final at Wimbledon, which he loses in four sets to Novak Djokovic. His run is not without controversy as he is twice fined for his behaviour, for spitting towards a spectator in his first-round match with Paul Jubb and for an audible obscenity during a fiery third-round encounter with Stefanos Tsitsipas.

January 2023: Undergoes knee surgery, beginning a prolonged period of injury problems that has limited him to only one Grand Slam appearance since.

February 2023: Has an assault charge dismissed by a magistrate after pleading guilty to shoving over his ex-girlfriend in 2021.

July 2023: Withdraws from Wimbledon because of a wrist injury, having hoped to match or even improve on his run to the final the prior year.

August 2026: Provisionally suspended after a sample given at an ATP tournament in Majorca in June tested positive for benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine.

articles.title: Badosa pierde con Coco Gauff en el US Open: "Paula es una jugadora difícil"
articles.standfirst: Coco Gauff se impuso a Paula Badosa en 6-4 y 7-6(5) en 1 hora y 59 minutos de partido, y espera en la siguiente ronda a la también española Cristina Bucsa
articles.summary: Coco Gauff se impuso a Paula Badosa en 6-4 y 7-6(5) en 1 hora y 59 minutos de partido, y espera en la siguiente ronda a la también española Cristina Bucsa
articles.body: La estadounidense Coco Gauff eliminó a la española Paula Badosa en la segunda ronda del US Open y se enfrentará en la tercera a la también española Cristina Bucsa. Gauff, cuarta del mundo y campeona en Nueva York en 2023, se impuso a Badosa, ahora 87 en el ranking, por 6-4 y 7-6(5) en 1 hora y 59 minutos de partido. Dos errores letales de Badosa, en sendas dejadas que se quedaron cortas y murieron en la red, le costaron 'breaks' en el séptimo juego del primer set y en el tercero del segundo. Parecía que Gauff tenía el partido bajo control en el segundo set, pero tres errores en sus subidas a la red en el octavo juego dieron una vida a Badosa, que logró su primer 'break' para igualar 4-4. Gauff volvió a romper para el 6-5 y sacar para el partido, pero Badosa se lo devolvió y forzó el desempate. Gauff se puso con dos bolas de partido tras una doble falta de la española. Badosa salvó la primera, pero Gauff selló la clasificación en la segunda. Badosa y Gauff llegaban al partido de este jueves con un balance de 8-5 favorable a la española, incluidos sus dos últimos enfrentamientos: en el torneo de Berlín de 2026 y en el Abierto de Australia de 2025. "Paula es una jugadora difícil. Sentía que tenía el partido bajo control, pero tampoco creo que hiciera demasiadas cosas mal. Ella subió el nivel. Estoy muy contenta de haber pasado hoy", explicó Gauff en declaraciones a pie de pista. "Vi el cuadro y, desde luego, no es alguien contra quien quieras jugar en segunda ronda. Fue número dos del mundo y es una gran competidora. Creo que necesito partidos así para ganar confianza", reconoció la estadounidense. La española Cristina Bucsa, número 40 de la WTA, se impuso a la japonesa Himeno Sakatsume (n.144) por 7-6(6), 6(0)-7 y 7-6(6) para avanzar a la tercera ronda del US Open. Bucsa necesitó tres horas y un minuto de partido para sellar su pase a la siguiente ronda, donde se enfrentará con Coco Gauff (n.4). La tenista española pudo rematar el primer set con 5-4 a su favor y turno de saque, pero acabó llevándoselo tras un desempate muy igualado en el que solo cedió una vez su servicio. El segundo tuvo un guion idéntico, solo que esta vez fue la jugadora nipona la que ganó un desempate mucho más holgado. El encuentro se decantó para Busca en el 'tie break' del tercero, después de que la española desaprovechara dos bolas de partido con saque y 5-4 arriba. Bucsa busca repetir los octavos de final que alcanzó en la última edición del Abierto de Estados Unidos, su mejor resultado en un 'Grand Slam' hasta la fecha.

articles.title: Kyrgios se libra tras dar positivo por cocaína: puede seguir jugando mientras lidia con sus demonios
articles.standfirst: Nick Kyrgios, autorizado a regresar tras determinar la ITIA que consumió cocaína fuera de competición
articles.summary: Nick Kyrgios, autorizado a regresar tras determinar la ITIA que consumió cocaína fuera de competición
articles.body: El australiano Nick Kyrgios podrá seguir jugando a tenis después de que las autoridades antidopaje determinaran que su prueba positiva por cocaína se produjo fuera de competición. El jugador de 31 años, exfinalista de Wimbledon, dio positivo por cocaína mientras disputaba un torneo ATP 250 en Mallorca el pasado mes de junio y comenzó una suspensión provisional el 4 de agosto. Oficialmente, tiene permiso para volver a jugar a partir de este viernes (ha disputado apenas tres torneos en cada uno de los dos últimos años, lastrado por lesiones en la rodilla y la muñeca que requirieron cirugía en ambos casos). Si la prueba se hubiera realizado durante una competición, Kyrgios podría haberse enfrentado a una suspensión de cuatro años. La cadena ESPN adelanta que la Agencia Internacional de Integridad del Tenis (ITIA) lo sancionó con tres meses de suspensión, plazo que se redujo a un mes a condición de que siguiera un programa de rehabilitación aprobado. En el momento de la suspensión Kyrgios califió el resultado positivo en el control como un "grave error" y describió la situación como una "llamada de atención", prometiendo "centrarse en recuperar el buen camino". "No voy a poner excusas, pero quiero contextualizar la situación en la que me encontraba. Los dos últimos años marcados por las lesiones han pasado una factura enorme", explicó. Nick Kyrgios confesó en una entrevista concedida en 2022 al canal australiano 'Nine' su lucha contra sus problemas de salud mental: "El equilibrio es algo con lo que me cuesta lidiar. Siempre he sido así desde que era un niño. Los partidos siempre fueron una montaña rusa". "Realmente me esfuerzo mucho. A veces es una lucha para mí. Algunos días me despierto y vengo a las pistas o me despierto y simplemente no quiero salir de mi habitación. Lidio con problemas humanos normales, pero también estoy orgulloso de mí mismo. Salgo, mantengo la cabeza baja y juego bien. No es fácil hacerlo semana tras semana"... soy dos personas muy diferentes en la pista y fuera de ella", explicó. Nick Kyrgios no dudó a la hora de contestar a cómo de graves fueron los problemas de salud mental que sufrió en 2019: "Fueron muy serios... hasta el punto hasta llegarme a autolesionar el brazo... y eso no está bien". El intenso dolor emocional llevó a Kyrgios a "cortarme y quemarme en una mierda bastante jodida". "Sentí que estaba decepcionando a la gente todo el tiempo. Me sentí inútil y odié mi vida en un momento", reconoció. "Supongo que alejé a todos los que se preocupaban por mí y no me estaba comunicando. Simplemente me cerré la vida real y estaba tratando de manejar y abordar mis problemas de frente. Estaba abusando mucho del alcohol y las drogas, y eso se salió fuera de control", reconoció el tenista australiano. En febrero de 2020 Kyrgios ya habló sobre su grave crisis personal de 2019: "Tenía pensamientos suicidas y estaba, literalmente, sufriendo para salir de la cama y jugar para millones de personas. Estaba solo, deprimido, negativo, abusando de alcohol y drogas que me alejaron de la familia y los amigos. No podía hablar con nadie o confiar en nadie".

articles.body: Karen Khachanov knocked out third seed Felix Auger-Aliassime from the US Open on Thursday, winning 6-7(5), 6-3, 6-2, 6-2 to reach the third round.The Russian, ranked No. 50 in the world, came into the tournament after losing the opening match in all three of his US Open warm-up events. But he took advantage of an off-colour Auger-Aliassime, whose level dropped as the match went on at Louis Armstrong Stadium.After the match, Auger-Aliassime said he started feeling unwell during the contest and struggled to recover."After a set and a half, I just couldn't feel well and was dizzy and seeing spots and couldn't recover," he said, as quoted by BBC. "I thought maybe it would pass, but it didn't."I've never felt quite like that. I've had cramps before. I've felt tired towards the end of matches, but in a normal way."This was abnormal a little bit, and there were no signs in the last couple of days and no signs this morning, as well."The defeat made Auger-Aliassime the highest-ranked player to exit the men's singles draw so far in New York.Khachanov, who reached the US Open semi-finals in 2022, broke the Canadian's serve seven times during the match. He also saved seven of the nine break points he faced.The win is only Khachanov's second victory over a top-10 player at a Grand Slam and sends him into the third round in New York.The result meant Khachanov has now reached the third round of all four Grand Slam tournaments in a single ​calendar year for the first time.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: El "zoo de l@s influencers" durante el US Open que amenaza al tenis: "Huele a marihuana en la pista"
articles.standfirst: El mal comportamiento del más de centenar de influencers acreditad@s por el US Open afecta a los partidos y provoca las quejas de l@s tenistas
articles.summary: El mal comportamiento del más de centenar de influencers acreditad@s por el US Open afecta a los partidos y provoca las quejas de l@s tenistas
articles.body: La tenista Naomi Osaka instó a los influencers que acuden al US Open a informarse sobre las normas para los espectadores, después de que su partido de primera ronda ante Anastasia Zakharova se viera interrumpido por un grupo ruidoso situado en uno de los palcos de lujo de la pista Arthur Ashe. La cuatro veces campeona de Grand Slam se disponía a sacar cuando el juez de silla llamó la atención a los ocupantes del palco, ya que parecían estar realizando una sesión de fotos improvisada: "Por favor, los del palco que está detrás de mí... les ruego que ocupen sus asientos". Dos días después Osaka, tras ganar a Katerina Siniakova, ha hablado del incidente de los influencers en el US Open: "Creo que, obviamente, si acudes a un evento deportivo, debes respetar el deporte... Y considero que es una cuestión de cortesía básica informarse sobre el deporte, especialmente en lo que respecta a la etiqueta". "Me parece bien que la gente contribuya a popularizar el tenis entre su público específico, pero creo que la situación debe gestionarse mucho mejor, sobre todo en partidos de primera ronda", apuntó. La estadounidense Jessica Pegula se mostró mucho menos diplomática que Osaka a la hora de hablar sobre el incidente con los influencers en la pista durante el US Open: "Hay gente ahí abajo intentando competir; es su carrera y su trabajo. Me parece un poco irrespetuoso... Me da la sensación de que este año la cosa se ha ido un poco de las manos". "En la Ashe se oye todo. Incluso cuando parece haber silencio, siempre hay un murmullo, gente hablando, comiendo, riendo y expresando toda clase de emociones. Realmente tienes que esforzarte por aislarte en tu propia burbuja cuando estás ahí fuera", describe. El tenista francés Adrian Mannarino también denunció el zoo humano en el que se han convertido las gradas del US Open por culpa de los influencers. "Huele a marihuana en la pista, se está convirtiendo en un zoológico. Son condiciones realmente inusuales. La gente entra como le da la gana, se mueve, habla... El torneo lo tolera, no sé si es lo mejor para los jugadores y para el deporte en general. Creo que hay muchas reglas que se podrían cambiar en el tenis, pero esta sin duda no es la que debería haberse cambiado ahora mismo", dijo tras perder contra Alexander Bublik por 6-3, 6-1 y 6-1. "La pista 17 huele como la sala de estar de Snoop Dogg. Dios mío, está en todas partes. Toda la cancha huele a hierba"... ", describió Zverev, actual número dos mundial. En 2025 Casper Ruud afirmó que en Nueva York, durante el US Open, "vayas donde vayas huele a marihuana y eso también se traslada a las pistas de tenis. Hay que aceptarlo, pero no es que sea mi olor favorito". En 2023 Maria Sakkari explotó por el fuerte olor a cannabis durante su partido en el US Open contra Rebeka Masarova y se quejó a la juez de silla. "Creo que era hierba (marihuana) y que el olor venía del parque", sentenciaba Sakkari. Masarova lo ratificó: "En 2021 jugué en esa pista con Svitolina y ya olía, lo que pasa es que no me afectó de manera negativa". Daniil Medvedev también ve con recelo esta evolución de la presencia de influencers en las gradas en los torneos de tenis. Le disgusta la idea de convertir el torneo en una especie de "Disneylandia del tenis". "Sigue siendo un deporte donde, en cierto modo, luchamos por nuestra supervivencia", alertó el tenista ruso. Las normas de etiqueta en el tenis dictan, por lo general, que los aficionados deben reservar las conversaciones y los desplazamientos para los cambios de lado de pista o las pausas entre sets, momentos en los que los jugadores están sentados en sus sillas. Pero 2024 el US Open adoptó una política de "libre circulación de aficionados", que permite a los espectadores moverse durante los puntos, independientemente de lo que ocurra en la pista. "La USTA se esfuerza constantemente por fomentar el tenis en Estados Unidos y atraer a nuevas audiencias a este deporte. El US Open es nuestra mejor oportunidad para lograrlo, y recibimos con los brazos abiertos a quienes se acercan por primera vez a nuestro evento. Queremos que todos nuestros aficionados e invitados disfruten de una experiencia increíble durante su visita, pero también debemos garantizar que no interfieran con la acción ni con la competición en la pista. Buscamos continuamente formas de asegurar que el público en las gradas sepa qué está permitido y qué está prohibido", explicó Brendan McIntyre, responsable de comunicación del US Open, al 'Daily Mail'. La apuesta del US Open por la presencia de influencers en YouTube, TikTok, Instagram o Substack en sus gradas se plasma en que este año este torneo del Grand Slam llegó a acreditar a 100 creadores de contenido.

articles.title: US Open: Coco Gauff overcomes Paula Badosa as Learner Tien brings curtain down on Gael Monfils' Grand Slam career
articles.summary: Cincinnati Open champion Coco Gauff continued her US Open charge by knocking out former world No 2 Paula Badosa; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app
articles.body:
The American fourth seed and 2023 US Open winner continues her path to the third round, where she will face ​Spaniard Cristina Bucsa .

On a sweltering evening that contrasted with the rain-hit opening days, Gauff took to Arthur ​Ashe Court with the backing of a partisan crowd and hopes of continuing her pursuit of a third Grand Slam title.

But it ​was no simple task against the world No 87, ‌who, despite the gulf in the rankings, holds a positive record over the American, including victories in ​their last two meetings - a straight-sets win at last year's Australian Open first round and more recently, during this summer's grass-court swing in Berlin.

Badosa threatened early to seize the initiative, forcing Gauff to save two break points. But the American struck with ‌the decisive break, aided by a costly forehand error from the Spaniard that appeared to rattle her both mentally and in her execution, as Gauff closed out ‌the opener to take the lead.

The second set proved just as much of a spectacle, with both players swapping breaks twice apiece before a tie-break was needed, Badosa raising her level as she searched for a way back into the match.

The breaker followed the same script until Badosa sent a long ball, ​prompting a euphoric celebration from Gauff as she sealed her ​place in the next round.

"Paula is a tough player. I feel ​like I had the lead but there wasn't too much I did ⁠wrong. She stepped it up. I'm really happy to be through today," the 22-year-old said on court.

"I saw the draw. Definitely not someone you want to play in the ⁠2nd round. Former number two in the world. ​Great competitor. I think I need matches like this to build my ​confidence. I'm happy with how I managed today. There was a bit of nerves."

French Open champion Mirra Andreeva eased into the ‌third round after sweeping past German Eva Lys with a 6-0 6-2 victory.

The 19-year-old will next face Czech Nikola Bartunkova .

World No 2 Elena Rybakina cruised past Spain's Jessica Bouzas Maneiro 6-2 6-4 in a little ‌over an hour to set up a clash against Ukraine's Yuliia Starodubtseva .

Rybakina had dispelled doubts ​over her fitness after retiring from the Cincinnati Open ​in the build-up to the tournament, saying: "It's true it wasn't perfect ⁠preparation at all. I was ​a bit upset watching everybody practice preparing for the tournament ​and I was just doing all possible recovery and gym. I'm super happy to be here."

Tien too good as Monfils makes final Grand Slam bow

Young American Learner Tien brought the ‌curtain down on Gael Monfils' Grand Slam career on Thursday as ‌the American youngster defeated the French veteran 6-3 6-4 ​6-3 in a clash of generations to reach the third ​round.

Monfils turned back the clock ‌to beat Adolfo Daniel Vallejo in the first round on ​his 40th birthday and extend his stay in New York, but the wildcard's run ended under ​lights against an opponent half ⁠his age.

On a muggy evening Monfils appeared ‌drained towards the end of the first set and turned to the crowd for inspiration, but ‌14th seed Tien was unfazed and tightened his grip on the contest.

With the opening set in the bag, 20-year-old Tien continued to dictate ⁠proceedings in the next, absorbing Monfils' ​bursts of aggression to clinch it ​and edge closer to the third ​round for a meeting with Czech Jakub Mensik .

Monfils ⁠made a final, emotion-fuelled charge in the third set with some trademark shot-making, but Tien ⁠stood his ground and sealed ​victory before warmly embracing the French showman ​who will retire at the end of the year.

The US Open is live on Sky Sports from August 30. Stream tennis with no contract on NOW and the Sky Sports App . You can also watch the Laver Cup at The O2 in London from 25-27 September live on Sky Sports.

articles.title: La tenista más rica del mundo denuncia la doble moral en el tenis
articles.standfirst: "Los jugadores no pueden aceptar patrocinios relacionados con las apuestas, pero los torneos obtienen beneficios de gran parte de esa actividad"
articles.summary: "Los jugadores no pueden aceptar patrocinios relacionados con las apuestas, pero los torneos obtienen beneficios de gran parte de esa actividad"
articles.body: Jessica Pegula, la tenista más rica del mundo, denuncia la doble moral del tenis en relación a las estrictas restricciones que tiene los tenistas respecto a los patrocinios relacionados con las apuestas, mientras que los torneos pueden lucrarse con acuerdos similares. "Es un tema que se viene discutiendo desde hace un tiempo. Los jugadores no pueden aceptar patrocinios relacionados con las apuestas, pero los torneos obtienen beneficios de gran parte de esa actividad", dijo la estadounidense de 32 años en relación a la asociación del US Open con Kalshi, una empresa de mercados de predicción. Jessica Pegula, que llegó a ser la número 1 del mundo en 2023, subrayó que "es una cuestión compleja, porque recibimos muchas críticas negativas de los apostadores, tanto si ganamos como si perdemos; a veces ni siquiera importa el resultado". El acoso de parte de los apostadores a los jugadores es una de las lacras que arrastra el tenis en los últimos años. 'Yahoo' publica que la nueva 'Matriz de Amenazas' (Threat Matrix) de la WTA indica que los apostadores frustrados son responsables de una parte significativa del acoso en línea que reciben las tenistas. "Recibimos muchos comentarios de odio en las redes sociales por este motivo. Resulta duro ver eso y, al mismo tiempo, encontrarse con que una de estas empresas es un gran patrocinador visible en la pista o en televisión" comentó Pegula. En 2024 la tenista francesa Caroline Garcia publicó algunos de los mensajes que recibió por parte de los acosadores digitales tras perder unos partidos: "Deberías considerar suicidarte", "Un payaso debería estar en el circo", "Espero que tu madre se muera pronto" o "Eres una porquería". Jessica Pegula reconoce que "las apuestas contribuyen en gran medida a mantener el interés de los aficionados, así que tengo sentimientos encontrados al respecto. Pero es interesante ver cómo empiezan a introducirse cada vez más en el mundo del tenis". Jessica Pegula ha ganado más de 26,1 millones de dólares durante su larga carrera en el tenis, es considerada la tenista más rica del mundo por la fortuna de su padre. La tenista estadounidense es hija de Terry Pegula, un magnate multimillonario de 75 años que es propietario y presidente de los Buffalo Bills (NFL) y Buffalo Sabres (NHL) y propietario de Rochester Americans (AHL), Buffalo Bandits (NLL) y Rochester Knighthawks (NLL). Pegula amasó su fortuna neta de más de 7.000 millones de dólares invirtiendo en operaciones de gas natural, bienes raíces, entretenimiento y deportes profesionales. Terry Pegula tiene cinco hijos que deberían heredar su inmensa fortuna y entramado empresarial.

articles.title: US Open: Alexander Zverev survives another 5-set marathon, making ominous history as top seed in the process
articles.summary: Alexander Zverev is still alive, after 10 hours of tennis.
articles.body:
Alexander Zverev is two matches into his first Grand Slam as the No. 1 seed. They have taken a total of 10 sets and more than nine hours.

After needing a five-set marathon to survive Lorenzo Sonego in the first round of the 2026 US Open, the German found himself again going the distance in a 6-4, 4-6, 7-6, 7-6, 6-3 win over Quentin Halys in the second round. His first match ended at 1:55 a.m. local time, his second at 2:15 a.m.

If that sounds unusual, it's because it's unprecedented. Zverev is the first top seed in the Open Era to begin a Grand Slam with back-to-back five-setters, per ESPN .

He quickly went shirtless to celebrate the win.

Zverev's play fluctuated throughout the match. He still had the enormous serve, notching 29 aces and winning 82-of-103 first-serve points (80%). He also needed an inordinate amount of tries in the match's biggest moments, going 5 for 20 on break points. He was 5 for 22 on break points against Sonego as well.

He was often passive at the baseline and at one point seemed to have lost significant power on his forehand, but also benefited from some wildly off-target shots from Halys, who finished the match with 63 unforced errors to Zverev's 49.

It was nowhere close to the form Zverev will need if he wants to show his Roland-Garros title earlier this year was no fluke. His third-round opponent will be No. 25 seed Alejandro Tabilo.

The US Open is wide open for Alexander Zverev, if he can just take it

Before Zverev took the court, Thursday was shaping up to be a very good day for him.

There were three notable upsets at Flushing Meadows on the men's side that day: No. 3 seed Felix Auger-Aliassime, No. 6 seed Alex de Minaur and No. 13 Lorenzo Musetti. We can call those players by a different name: the highest possible seeds Zverev could have faced in the semifinals, quarterfinals and fourth round.

At this point, the highest seeds in front of Zverev before the semifinals are No. 21 Luciano Darderi in the fourth round and No. 31 seed Zizou Bergs in the quarterfinals.

We've seen this movie before. Zverev won Roland-Garros partially thanks to a field depleted of contenders, and we're already getting close to that point in New York. In addition to Auger-Aliassime and de Minaur, No. 4 seed Novak Djokovic went down in the first round, as did two of the most intriguing young players in the field in No. 10 Arthur Fils and No. 12 Rafael Jodar.

No. 2 Carlos Alcaraz is still out there, but playing his first tournament in more than four months. Jannik Sinner, who has beaten Zverev 10 times in a row, pulled out of the draw with a knee injury.

There remain some threats in the field, most notably No. 7 Daniil Medvedev, who won the US Open in 2021, and a collection of talented Americans headlined by No. 8 Ben Shelton, No. 9 Taylor Fritz and No. 11 Frances Tiafoe.

The flip side of this is that Zverev has so far looked so vulnerable that this could be the best chance in years for an American man to break the 23-year drought since the country's last Grand Slam, Andy Roddick's US Open title in 2003.

Roddick spent the Zverev match serving as color commentator in the ESPN booth.

articles.title: US Open 2026: Naomi Osaka and Jessica Pegula on influencers causing disruption in New York
articles.summary: The behaviour of influencers and content creators has become a major talking point at this year's US Open amid incidents of matches being disrupted.
articles.body:
When it comes to etiquette in tennis, there are a fair few unwritten rules.

Apologising after winning a point from a net cord. Honesty around line calls, double bounces and double-hits. Post-match handshakes.

As for the spectators, it is common courtesy not to disturb the players during points.

Around 100 influencers and content creators have been granted accreditation for the tournament in New York - double the amount from last year.

Their presence has led to debate over how to balance bringing tennis to a new, different audience while respecting the game's etiquette.

"I definitely think it's cool to have a new demographic and I definitely think it helps grow the sport," world number four Coco Gauff said.

"But if you're being invited to a red carpet, you wouldn't show up in jeans.

"I think it's just follow the etiquette of the sport. That's all."

During two-time champion Naomi Osaka's first-round match on Arthur Ashe Stadium, one group held a photo shoot in their hospitality suite while play was going on.

The group turned on a portable ring light while Osaka was serving, leading to a reprimand from the umpire.

When Osaka returned on Thursday, the umpire had to remind the crowd several times to be quiet.

"Today the umpire told everyone to be quiet more than I've ever heard an umpire tell a crowd to be quiet," Osaka said.

"I tell people I normally just focus on the match and the court, but there was a moment where there was people shouting and you could hear it quite clearly.

In one video, which has gone viral, a group can be seen speaking loudly as they film themselves during Osaka's first-round match on Tuesday, which led to the chair umpire calling for them to stop.

"I think obviously if you come to a sporting event, you have to respect the sport," Osaka said.

"I feel like it's common courtesy to read up on the sport, especially the etiquette.

"It could be a good thing for people to make the sport of tennis popular to their specific audience, but I think it has to be managed a lot better, especially in the situation like my first-round match.

"Overall, I think there are huge positives. You want people to continue to grow the sport.

"I just think it has to be in a way that everyone knows the rules and the etiquette."

No Britons left in US Open singles as Dart & Jones lose

'More upside than downside' or 'a little too much'?

Arthur Ashe is the biggest tennis stadium in the world, and matches are often accompanied by a buzz of noise from conversations around the arena.

Men's seventh seed Daniil Medvedev, who has had a tricky relationship with the New York crowds in the past, believes whatever brings more eyes to tennis can only be a good thing.

"I think the more we try to raise awareness about tennis, the better it is, the more popular the sport is," the Russian said.

"The more the sport grows, the better it is. I trust USTA [tournament organisers the United States Tennis Association] with what they are doing.

"I think [there is] a lot more upside than downside, so go for it."

American 11th seed Frances Tiafoe praised the diversity of the crowd in New York.

"I think the Open is great because you get all types of people that want to come and watch tennis," he said.

"All different walks of life, different types of people, different type of occupations. Personally, I love that.

"I have no problem with anybody doing anything, coming to watch the tennis."

American world number three Jessica Pegula, however, said some of the behaviour had been "disrespectful".

"I can appreciate the influencers coming and showcasing the US Open experience," Pegula said.

"But I do think that it's tough when you see videos when they're taking pictures and using the selfie lights.

"People are down there trying to perform. It's their career and their job. It seems a bit disrespectful.

"I think it's become a little too much this year.

"I can appreciate one side of it, but I think when you have the other side literally interrupting matches, it gets a little tough."

The US Open introduced a policy of free fan movement in 2024, meaning fans no longer have to wait to take their seats during changeovers.

A year later, the tournament was expanded to 15 days. The week before the singles draw is now marketed as a 'Fan Week', showcasing the revamped mixed doubles competition and exhibition matches between players past and present.

It is all part of what tournament chief executive Craig Tiley hopes will become "the tennis Disneyland".

Tiley, asked about influencers being accredited in a pre-tournament news conference, said: "We need to find ways of reaching new audiences, reaching people in a way that they connect with media today.

"The creation of the creator credential has been a key part of that because it's enabled us to talk to people in a way that they're listening. That's been a big focus."

Since the incident in Osaka's first match, there has been increased messaging on screens around the ground reminding people to "refrain from any activity that could disrupt the game, including noise levels, flash photography and ring lights".

The USTA said in a statement it "is always striving to grow tennis in this country and bring new audiences into the sport".

"We want all of our fans and guests to have an incredible time when they attend, but we also need to ensure they do not interfere with the action and competition on the court," it added.

"We are continually looking for ways to ensure fans in the stands know what is permitted and what is prohibited."

articles.title: Zverev goes distance to scrape into third round as upsets rock US Open
articles.summary: Men’s third seed Felix Auger-Aliassime goes out, along with sixth-seed Alex de Minaur and 13th-seed Lorenzo Musetti.
articles.body:
Top-seeded Alexander Zverev kept his bid for a first US Open title on track with a gritty five-set victory over Quentin Halys, staying the course as a spate of upsets rocked the men’s draw on Thursday.

A trio of former women’s champions – Coco Gauff, Iga Swiatek and Naomi Osaka – booked third-round berths, along with reigning Grand Slam champions Elena Rybakina and Mirra Andreeva.

But men’s third seed Felix Auger-Aliassime tumbled out, along with sixth-seeded Alex de Minaur and 13th-seeded Lorenzo Musetti.

Zverev laboured until 2:15 am Friday on Arthur Ashe Stadium to shake off 52nd-ranked Frenchman Halys 6-4, 4-6, 7-6 (7/3), 6-7 (3/7), 6-3.

The four-hour 33-minute marathon followed his wild first-round five-setter against 89th-ranked Lorenzo Sonego that kept Zverev at it until shortly before 2am (06:00 GMT) on Wednesday.

“The performance was quite s*** to be honest, but I won, that’s the most important thing,” Zverev said afterwards.

“Physically, I feel fine. I am proud, I think, to be physically quite strong. I just hope at some point I’ll start playing better tennis.

“I’m winning ugly right now. It’s also a skill to win ugly and when you’re not playing great tennis. I think I’ve mastered that right now.”

While Zverev survived, Auger-Aliassime fell 6-7 (5/7), 6-3, 6-2, 6-2 to 50th-ranked Russian Karen Khachanov, who pulled away relentlessly from the physically ailing Canadian, who said he was “dizzy and seeing spots”.

“I thought maybe it would pass, but it didn’t,” a dejected Auger-Aliassime said.

Khachanov took full advantage of 47 unforced errors, with eight double faults, from Auger-Aliassime, who struggled particularly on serve.

“I thought maybe he had some physical issues; it’s part of our sport,” Khachanov said. “From my side I tried to give my best performance, fighting, fighting.”

De Minaur fell to Botic van de Zandschulp 6-4, 7-5, 6-2, while 123rd-ranked Australian Dane Sweeny shocked 13th seed Musetti 3-6, 6-1, 6-2, 6-2 to reach the third round of a major for the first time.

It is not the first time Van de Zandschulp has sprung an upset at Flushing Meadows, where he shocked Carlos Alcaraz in the second round in 2024.

Meanwhile, top women contenders marched on.

Fourth-seeded Gauff, the 2023 champion, thrilled the Ashe night crowd with a 6-4, 7-6 (7/5) victory over former world number two Paula Badosa of Spain.

Swiatek sailed through with a 6-3, 6-2 victory over Nadia Podoroska, while Osaka survived a second-set swoon to beat Katerina Siniakova 6-2, 5-7, 6-1.

Australian Open winner Rybakina, the world number two who is closing in on Aryna Sabalenka’s number one ranking, saw off Spain’s Jessica Bouzas Maneiro 6-2, 6-4, and Andreeva rolled over Germany’s Eva Lys 6-0, 6-2.

Gauff, 22, had lost five of her eight prior meetings with Badosa, so she was ready when the Spaniard piled on the pressure in the second set, regaining a break to force the tiebreaker.

“I knew she would raise her level. She’s capable of blasting winners and blasting return winners,” said Gauff, who was pleased she kept her composure.

“I think I need matches like this to build my confidence,” the 2023 US Open winner said.

Swiatek, whose six Grand Slam titles include the 2022 US Open, had things mostly her own way against Podroska, a former top-40 player now 449th in the world.

She fought off four break points at 5-3 in the first set, then pulled away to polish off the win in little more than an hour.

Japan’s Osaka, who counts two US Open titles among her four majors, looked in total control against Siniakova as she raced through the first set and to a 4-2 lead in the second without facing a break point.

But the Japanese star’s unforced errors began to pile up, and doubles world number one Siniakova pounced to climb from 5-3 down and take the set.

Osaka regrouped in the decider, riding a quick break to a 3-0 lead and fending off a pair of break points on the way to victory.

“I just felt like I had to fight,” she said.

So did former Australian Open champion Madison Keys, who saved five match points to beat Anna Bondar 4-7, 6-4, 7-6 (10/5).

There was a bittersweet goodbye on Louis Armstrong Stadium, where 20-year-old American Learner Tien ended 40-year-old Gael Monfils’s Grand Slam career with a 6-3, 6-4, 6-3 victory.

“It’s been a long ride,” Monfils told an adoring New York crowd. “You are my second-best crowd. Of course, it can’t top Paris, but you are up there!”

articles.title: Zverev necesita otros cinco sets para alcanzar la tercera ronda
articles.standfirst: El número 2 del mundo y primer cabeza de serie en Nueva York derrotó al francés Halys tras cuatro horas y 33 minutos en cancha
articles.summary: El número 2 del mundo y primer cabeza de serie en Nueva York derrotó al francés Halys tras cuatro horas y 33 minutos en cancha
articles.body: El alemán Alexander Zverev volvió a necesitar cinco sets este jueves, ante el francés Quentin Halys, para avanzar a la tercera ronda del Abierto de Estados Unidos, en una jornada en la que Félix Auger-Aliassime y Alex de Miñaur quedaron eliminados, mientras Gael Monfils se despidió de Nueva York a las puertas de su retirada. Zverev, número 2 del mundo y primer cabeza de serie en Nueva York, derrotó a Halys, número 52, por 6-4, 4-6, 7-6(3), 6(3)-7 y 6-3 tras 4 horas y 33 minutos en cancha. Eran las 02:15 del viernes cuando terminó el partido en Nueva York. Es la primera ves que un primer cabeza de serie juega dos partidos a cinco sets en las dos primeras rondas de un 'Grand Slam'. Zverev ha invertido 9 horas y 26 minutos en estas dos primeras rondas, con un desgaste muy grande contra rivales muy inferiores en el ranking. "He ganado, eso es lo más importante. He vuelto a estar aquí otras cuatro horas y media, otra vez hasta las 02:15 de la madrugada. Pero para eso voy al gimnasio y para eso entreno en pista. Para eso trabajo cada día: para estar preparado y poder salir adelante en momentos tan difíciles", dijo Zverev. El alemán se medirá en tercera ronda al chileno Alejandro Tabilo, número 28 del mundo. La jornada de este jueves también dejó la eliminación en el cuadro masculino del canadiense Auger-Aliassime (n.4) y del australiano De Miñaur (n.7), que se suman a la del serbio Novak Djokovic (n.5) en una criba temprana de tenistas del 'Top 10'. Auger-Aliassime cayó a manos del ruso Karen Khachanov (n.50) y De Miñaur perdió ante el neerlandés Botic van de Zandschulp (n.70). En cambio, el italiano Flavio Cobolli (n.6) y el estadounidense Taylor Fritz (n.10) sí lograron avanzar a tercera ronda. Monfils, de 40 años, se despidió de Nueva York, el último 'grande' de su carrera, a la que pondrá fin en unas semanas en el Masters 1.000 de París. El francés, en su decimoctava aparición en el Abierto de Estados Unidos, cayó por 6-3, 6-4 y 6-3 ante el estadounidense Learner Tien, que ya le había derrotado en agosto en Montreal. "Ha sido un auténtico honor para mí jugar todos estos años delante de vosotros. Lo he dado todo e intentado ofrecer un tenis de alto nivel, pero también daros un gran espectáculo", dijo en su despedida Monfils, muy querido por la afición neoyorquina. A diferencia del masculino, el cuadro femenino sigue intacto de favoritas, entre ellas la kazaja Elena Rybakina (n.2) y la estadounidense Coco Gauff (n.4), que este jueves eliminaron, respectivamente, a las españolas Paula Badosa y Jessica Bouzas. También pasaron a tercera ronda la rusa Mirra Andreeva (n.5), la polaca Iga Swiatek (n.8) y la estadounidense Amanda Anisimova (n.10), además de la japonesa Naomi Osaka (n.13) o la filipina Alexandra Eala (n.18). Gauff se enfrentará el sábado en tercera ronda a Cristina Bucsa, única española con vida en el torneo.

articles.body: El tenis femenino español se ha quedado con Cristina Bucsa como única representante en el cuadro individual femenino del US Open. La culpa la tienen las eliminaciones de Paula Badosa a manos de Coco Gauff y Jessica Bouzas, que tampoco pudo con Elena Rybakina al ceder por 6-2 y 6-4. Esta última se ha recuperado a tiempo de sus problemas en el talón que la obligaron a abandonar en los cuartos de Cincinnati con Iga Swiatek. Tanto Gauff como Rybakina siguen en la carrera por el título y el numero 1 al final del tormeo. Gauff necesita ganar para liderar las listas de la WTA. A Rybakina, en cambio, le valen las semifinales. Eso significa que está a tres victorias de relevar a Aryna Sabalenka en lo más alto y convertirse en la trigésima jugadora que ocupa el primer puesto del ranking.

articles.title: 'Laban Alex': From a basketball- and boxing-obsessed nation where sporting heroes are mostly men, Filipina Alex Eala is creating a fandom of her own at US Open
articles.summary: Tennis News: The Alex Eala phenomenon is getting louder at Flushing Meadows — and, remarkably, it is no longer confined to the match courts.Hours before the Filipi.
articles.body: The Alex Eala phenomenon is getting louder at Flushing Meadows — and, remarkably, it is no longer confined to the match courts.Hours before the Filipina star was due to begin her US Open campaign, fans had already packed the practice courts, many of them without tickets for her evening match. They came carrying Philippine flags, wearing blue caps emblazoned with “Laban Alex” — a rallying cry meaning “Fight, Alex” — and turning a routine practice session into something resembling a main-event sporting spectacle.They watched every forehand and backhand, recorded her serves and volleys on their phones and cheered as though Eala were already competing for a Grand Slam title.That is the scale of the fandom the 21-year-old has created in a country where basketball and boxing have traditionally dominated the sporting landscape, and where many of the biggest sporting heroes have been men.Eala is changing that conversation.Her rise has not only given Filipino tennis fans a player to follow. It has created a new generation of supporters who see themselves in a young woman competing — and succeeding — on one of the biggest stages in world sport.And as Eala continues to progress at the US Open, the noise around her is only growing.From junior champion to one of the world's rising starsFour years ago, Eala announced herself to the tennis world in the very same city.In 2022, she became the first Filipino to win a junior Grand Slam singles title when she lifted the girls' singles trophy at the US Open. At the time, it was a landmark achievement for Philippine tennis, but few could have imagined how quickly her profile would grow in the years that followed.Her transition into the senior game has been gradual but increasingly spectacular.Last year, Eala gave the New York crowd an early glimpse of what she could become when she produced a remarkable comeback against then world No. 14 Clara Tauson. Down 1-5 in the deciding set, she fought her way back to win, sending more than 8,000 spectators in the Grandstand into a frenzy as Filipino flags waved around the stadium.It was more than a memorable victory. It was a preview of the connection Eala was beginning to build with her country's diaspora and with fans back home.She reached the second round of the US Open last year.Twelve months later, she is no longer simply the exciting young player from the Philippines.She is the world No. 18 and the No. 17 seed in New York, returning to Flushing Meadows as one of the most talked-about young players on the women's tour.And this time, she has gone one step further.Another breakthrough at Flushing MeadowsEala's latest US Open run began with a victory over American qualifier Mary Stoiana.She followed that up Thursday by powering past Ukraine's Oleksandra Oliynykova 6-1, 6-4, securing a place in the third round of the tournament for the first time.The victory also carried an element of redemption. Oliynykova had defeated Eala in three sets at the Strasbourg Open in May, but there was little doubt about the outcome this time.Eala immediately seized control, racing to a 4-0 lead in the opening set. Even after Oliynykova managed to get on the scoreboard with a break, Eala responded immediately and closed out the set 6-1.Her first serve was particularly effective, with Eala winning 10 of 12 points behind it in the opening set.The second set was more competitive, but Eala repeatedly found the decisive moments. After exchanging breaks, she produced another breakthrough in the seventh game and held her nerve to move within a game of victory.Oliynykova delayed the inevitable by holding serve, but Eala completed the job in the 10th game.The numbers reflected her authority. She produced 19 winners to Oliynykova's six and never allowed the match to drift away from her control.Her reward is a third-round meeting with her close friend Iva Jovic, who defeated Fran Jones in straight sets.For Eala, it is another significant marker in a season that has transformed her career.A season that has changed everythingThe US Open is only the latest chapter in what has been a stunning 2026 for Eala.Earlier this year, she reached the fourth round of a Grand Slam and made history by becoming the first Filipino to reach the semifinals of a WTA 1000 tournament.She then produced perhaps the biggest statement of her career at Wimbledon by defeating former world No. 1 Iga Swiatek.And in Washington, she went all the way.Eala recovered from a set down against Jessica Pegula in the final to become the first Filipino to win a WTA Tour singles title.That victory was historic on several levels. She became the first Filipino to win a singles title on the WTA Tour and, soon after, climbed to world No. 18 on August 24.In doing so, she became the highest-ranked Filipino and Southeast Asian tennis player in WTA Tour history and the first Filipino to break into the world's top 20.Her list of firsts has continued to expand: first Filipino to defeat a top-10 opponent, first to reach the fourth round of a major, first to reach the semifinals of a WTA 1000 event and now the first to win a WTA singles title.The trajectory explains why the attention surrounding her in New York feels so different this year.'Laban Alex' becomes a movementThe most striking evidence of Eala's popularity is not necessarily found inside the stadium. It can be seen at the practice courts.Fans have travelled from across the United States to watch her train. Some have driven for hours. Others have arrived without tickets simply hoping to catch a glimpse of her.For some Filipino-American supporters, Eala has made tennis personal in a way few other players have.Her age, her background, her ability to speak Tagalog and her unapologetic pride in representing the Philippines have helped supporters identify with her.Some fans who had never considered themselves serious tennis followers have begun watching the sport because of Eala. Families have started following her matches together. Older supporters have travelled to New York carrying Philippine flags, while younger fans have turned “Laban Alex” into their own soundtrack for her matches.It is a distinctly Filipino expression of sporting support — emotional, communal and increasingly impossible to ignore.Eala's achievements are also resonating because Filipinos have historically rallied strongly around athletes who break through on the international stage.The country's pride in Olympic champions such as gymnast Carlos Yulo has shown how quickly individual sporting success can become a national celebration.Eala is now creating something similar in tennis. The difference is that her story is still being written.The next chapter could be even biggerEala has been careful to keep the attention in perspective.Her rapid rise has brought her into the company of some of the biggest names in tennis, including former champions and world No. 1s. Partnerships and practice sessions with players such as Venus Williams and Naomi Osaka have given her an opportunity to learn from the sport's history while experiencing first-hand what it takes to remain at the highest level.Her success has also forced the tennis world to take notice.Former players and analysts have praised the improvement in her game, particularly over the past year, while marvelling at the size and intensity of the crowds she attracts.At just 21, Eala is already a Grand Slam junior champion, a WTA tournament winner, a top-20 player and a player capable of beating the very best.Yet perhaps the most remarkable part of her US Open story is that the tournament itself appears to be growing with her.Four years ago, she was a junior champion celebrating her first major breakthrough. Last year, she was the young Filipina who stunned Tauson and reached the second round. This year, she returned as a seeded player ranked inside the world's top 20.Now she is through to the third round.And around her, the Filipino flags are multiplying, the practice courts are filling up and the chants of “Laban Alex” are getting louder.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: US Open Influencer Credentials Double, And Tennis Etiquette Cracks
articles.summary: The U.S. Open nearly doubled its creator credentials to close to 100 this year. A halted Osaka match and viral ring-light clips show the cost of reach withou...
articles.body:
The chair umpire had to stop the match. During Naomi Osaka's first-round win at the U.S. Open on Monday, Kader Nouni paused play to ask a group in a hospitality suite behind his chair to sit down; they had been moving around and shooting photos, with a light, as Osaka prepared to serve. By midweek, clips of spectators holding ring lights during matches at Arthur Ashe Stadium were circulating widely, and the sport's most codified major had a new argument on its hands.

That argument is not really about tennis manners. It is about what happens when an institution built on silence between points invites in an audience whose job is to make noise.

The United States Tennis Association credentialed content creators as media for the first time in 2025, when it approved 54. This year, Front Office Sports reported the tournament approved close to 100 before qualifying week, and is separately paying roughly two dozen creators to produce content on the tournament's behalf across its three-week run. The USTA's own figure for last year's cohort: more than 5.5 million social engagements, according to Axios .

The commercial logic is not subtle. The 2025 U.S. Open drew 1.14 million fans, a 9% increase on the tournament's first million-fan year in 2024. Average ticket prices for the first day of main-draw play reached $296, up nearly 20% year over year, per TicketData figures cited by Front Office Sports. The tournament has become the place where fashion, finance and Hollywood go to be photographed, and creators are the people holding the cameras.

Players are split, but not the way you might expect

The top of the women's game is largely on the creators' side. World No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka told Front Office Sports she loves the attention: "It's more eyes on our sport." Former U.S. Open champion Daniil Medvedev said Wednesday the creator wave has brought tennis more upside than downside, and that he trusts the USTA to manage it — adding that a spectator who disrupts play with a light will likely be told to stop after the first time.

Jessica Pegula, the American world No. 3 and one of the tour's most active player representatives, has drawn a finer line. Weeks ago she credited influencers with helping grow the sport and making it trendier. After her second-round win Wednesday, asked about the ring-light videos, she said the behavior had gotten to be a little too much and called interruptions during play "a bit disrespectful" . Her distinction is worth keeping: creators showcasing the food, the merchandise and the fan experience is one thing; creators interrupting the match is another.

The former players are less enthusiastic, and their complaint is economic rather than aesthetic. Patrick McEnroe told Front Office Sports that the real tennis fan is starting to get priced out. Genie Bouchard said she is of two minds: she wants true fans to be able to go, and if brands and influencers are taking those seats, that comes with some sadness.

Here is the detail that matters for anyone running a brand, an event or a creator program: the people in the suite behind Nouni's chair were not there on U.S. Open creator credentials, tournament spokesperson Brendan McIntyre confirmed to Axios. They were guests. The credentialed creator program, whatever its flaws, did not produce the week's most viral etiquette failure. Hospitality did.

That shifts the accountability question. The USTA has said it reminds ticket holders and suite holders in advance to avoid anything that disrupts play, repeats the message on video boards, and lets chair umpires address the crowd when it crosses a line, much as they do with noise. It did not answer Front Office Sports' question about whether it is considering a ban on equipment like ring lights and flash cameras.

Kyle Hjelmeseth, founder of the creator talent agency G&B, made the sharper point to Axios: some creators know the institutional rules and ignore them, some never learned them, and once a brand or sponsor is in the mix, it is that brand's job to make sure everyone in the campaign understands the expected decorum. In other words, the ring light is a briefing failure before it is a behavior failure.

Tennis is not the only sport working this out. The ATP signed a global partnership with TikTok last August aimed at Gen Z and millennial fans through creator collaborations, and hosted its first Creator Summit in New York last week. The WTA launched its own creator program early this year. Front Office Sports reported this week that high school football administrators are now dealing with what they call the "pajama paparazzi" on their sidelines. Every rights holder chasing younger audiences is making the same trade: reach in exchange for control.

The U.S. Open's version of the trade is simply more visible, because the sport's norms are stricter and its cameras are everywhere. A ring light in a suite at Flushing Meadows is a small thing. What it exposes is not: the gap between inviting new messengers into a room and teaching them how the room works.

The USTA doubled the invitations this year. The lesson from Monday night is that the onboarding did not double with them.

articles.title: Venus and Serena Williams owe no one an explanation at US Open | Opinion
articles.summary: Critics are questioning the Williams sisters' US Open wild card, but the tennis legends are ready to play.
articles.body:
NEW YORK — Chances are that if you are not on a computer, whatever method or device you are reading this on had not been invented yet in the years that Venus and Serena Williams made their US Open main draw debuts.

Those years, 1997 for Venus and the following year for Serena, signified a changing of the guard in how tennis looks and is played, leading to more braids and beads, fewer serves and volleys, and the thundering echoes of "Come on!" whether it was an unforced error or a powerful winner leaving the opponents shaking their heads in bewilderment.

The strength, the muscles, the flair, the skills, and, most importantly, the championships that have followed both sisters from the streets of Compton, California, put them on a historic rise that they have yet to come down from three decades later.

Older, wiser, and no doubt with diminished skills, the sisters will make their tournament return to play in doubles for the first time in Flushing Meadows since 2022.

That entry came via a wild card courtesy of the United States Tennis Association, and also came with the virtual side-eye from those, mostly keyboard warriors, who don't matter in any way, shape, or form, opining about when or if an athlete should retire.

The quick answer to when some athletes should retire, especially in this reference to the Williams sisters, is whenever they damn well please.

The same can be said about Novak Djokovic, who doesn't turn 40 until next May. Let the 24-time Grand Slam winner continue to backhand, limp around, and throw up on the sidelines until he is ready to put down his racket for good.

Unforgettable US Open 2026 tennis photos from New York

But if you don't like that a 46-year-old and her 44-year-old sister are playing tennis on the biggest stage, there is an off button you can use on that aforementioned device. The critics would say they are too old and that no one wants to see them keep losing, most likely referring to Venus' singles record this year, where she hasn't won once and is currently on a 15-match losing streak.

And there is also the issue of the wild card entry, which can be used at the discretion of the tournament officials. Why didn't those same officials give that entry to another team?

The quick answer is that they don't want to or have to, and will continue to, like any other WTA tournament officials who have brains that are functioning, give out wild cards to the 14 Grand Slam doubles champions (including two at the US Open) as long as they are healthy and willing to play.

And the complaints from fans, journalists, and anyone else who has a problem with the Williams sisters' place in the field aren't enough to slow this gravy train and will continue to fall on deaf ears, because the USTA is a non-profit that continues to make millions of dollars, and not one high-profile athlete currently on tour has publicly complained about their entry in the tournament.

This is a simple case of selective complaining about an issue that isn't hurting anyone, and just because you have a Constitutional right, along with a mouth and hands, to spew and type utter nonsense, doesn't mean you can't be called out for stupidity.

When the sisters take center stage on Arthur Ashe Stadium in their first-round match against Hao-Ching Chan and Maya Joint, who beat Serena in singles at Wimbledon in June, guess who else won't be complaining?

If not for the Williams sisters' entry, the No. 14 seed probably wouldn't have snuffed Arthur Ashe Stadium, unless they make it all the way to the doubles final on Sept. 11. You can't buy that kind of exposure.

The truth is, the USTA and ESPN, who will televise this match in primetime, aren't stupid, at least on this issue. They could have put any other player or team in that coveted 7 p.m. ET spot, or relegated the Williams sisters to a court on the outskirts of the Billie Jean King Tennis Center. But the more eyes on greatness equals more money and more chances to brag about ratings.

Tennis, like every other sport, is in the entertainment business, which means no one is forcing anyone to watch, and Venus and Serena certainly don't need the $35,000 they will split just for showing up.

To their credit, the sisters probably don't care what people think. The nearly 24,000 fans who will show up to Arthur Ashe Stadium won't care either. They want to be entertained, be told by the chair umpire to shut up between points, drink their Honey Deuces, and then watch another rising star, Ben Shelton, take the Ashe stage against Denis Shapovalov in a third-round clash.

For those who dislike it, too bad, because this isn't the end of the GOAT and her big sister on your screen.

"We've waited a long time to get back on the doubles court. Eventually, we find our way to each other," Venus said. "We give each other so much grace and encouragement. This is our first time playing together in forever, and I think we're really getting into our stride."

Serena has been ramping up her activity for more singles competition.

"I probably will play again. I have to. After some of those returns, I think I need to play at least once," Williams said this week on "Good Morning America." "It's just also really wanting my children to see me play at a different age."

That alone is reason enough to watch. Game, set, match for the Williams sisters, no matter who wins on Friday.

articles.title: US Open influencers get credentials revoked after online flex goes wrong
articles.summary: After influencers Meg Radice and Audrey Jongens showed their US Open credentials online, the tournament revoked them. Radice and Jongens are begging for rein...
articles.body:
Social media influencers also known as content creators have been a hot topic at the 2026 US Open . The tournament began giving credentials to influencers in 2025, issuing 54. That number has nearly doubled, to 100, in 2026.

Tennis is trying to grow its fanbase. Some, including Daniil Medvedev , are embracing this move to include content creators, others believe it is a big mistake. Those opposed believe it is driving away the geniune fans of the sport and replacing them with people only there to sip Honey Deuces and record the experience.

A pair of credentialed US Open influencers named Meg Radice and Audrey Jongens, allegedly excited to share their experience, shared their credentials in a video. That was followed by immediate tournament action to promptly revoke them. Radice and Jongens share an Instagram page called theviplist with 154,000 followers.

Meg Radice and Audrey Jongens want credentials reinstated

TMZ reported that Radice and Jongens are making public pleas to the tournament to reinstate their credentials as they had blocked off the entire two weeks to go to and record content at all US Open events.

They did not realize they did anything wrong. The US Open likely reacted swiftly because anyone could screenshot and produce a copy of the credentials pictured to gain entry.

September 3, 2026; New York, United States; Japan's Naomi Osaka acknowledges fans after winning her second round match against Czech Republic's Katerina Siniakova. Mandatory Credit: Robert Deutsch-Imagn Images

This is another example of credentialed influencers being disruptive at the tournament. The umpire at Naomi Osaka's first round night match had to address a group who were filming live video with lights as the match was being played.

Is US Open losing its luster partly because of influencer influx?

Some believe the antics of the credentialed influencers is tarnishing the tournament. It is unclear if the US Open will continue to embrace influencers to the level it has this year in future years.
